newsitem.title: UK: British business group warns against windfall tax.
newsitem.headline: British business group warns against windfall tax.

text.p: Britain's Institute of Directors said on Thursday that the opposition Labour party's proposed "windfall" tax on utilities had difficulties and a better alternative would be increasing competition.

"The windfall tax is a very tempting option for Labour, but there are clear difficulties with it. Encouraging competition would be a better way forward," Richard Baron, the IoD's taxation executive, said in a statement.
Labour has proposed a one-off windfall tax on excess profits of utilities which would be used to create jobs for young people.
The IoD acknowledged that "some of the utilities do have spare funds at the moment," and added that public spending ought to be financed from tax revenues rather than borrowing.
But it said difficulties over a windfall tax included porblems over calculating who should pay and what amounts.

In addition, the IoD argued, increased tax revenue could alternatively be generated by allowing companies to reinvest profits or by distributing to shareholders who would spend or save, thereby contributing to tax takes.
The IoD said customers of utilities might suffer because under a windfall tax, money for investment might have to come from increased charges to customers.

It said a better approach would be to tighten up regulation to control excess profits and long-term to make industries more competitive and encourage efficiency, triggering increased profits and therefore higher corporation tax.
